newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Khrunichev, DASA in lightweight satellite venture.
newsitem.headline: Khrunichev, DASA in lightweight satellite venture.

text.p: Russia's Khrunichev Space Centre (KSC) and Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa) plan to cooperate in launching lightsweight satellites using a Russian-made launch vehicle, a KSC spokesman said on Thursday.
Sergei Zhiltsov told Reuters the two companies have signed an additional agreement which would allow them to develop a two-year-old project known as "Eurockot".
"We have got guarantees from Dasa to finance the first part of the Eurockot project," he said in a telephone interview.
Dasa's statement confirmed that the additional agreement with Khrunichev was signed.
The statement quoted Peter Bamberg, head of the Eurockot programme, who said that the first launch of three-stage launch vehicle was expected in 1998 from the Plesetsk launch site in northern Russia.
"Market research shows that Rokot boosters meet the world demand for launches of light satellites," the statement said.

In 1994 both firms set up a Eurockot Launch Services GMBH joint venture and Dasa promised to invest $30 million for the first part of it. But this May KSC said it wanted to end cooperation with its German partner because it had invested only $2 million.
"Now we have reached a mutual understanding to re-start our cooperation," Zhiltsov said.
The "Rokot" rocket is a modified SS-19 intercontinental millitary booster which can lift civil satellites weighting between 250 and 1,800 kg into orbit.

Zhiltsov said KSC owned 14 such rockets. "We only need to equip them with a third stage with adaptors for Western-made satellites and to modernise a launch pad on the cosmodrome," he said, adding that Dasa would undertake marketing and look for clients for launches.
He also said that the joint venture had no firm orders for launches yet.
